Title: When was the Golden Gate Bridge built?
Answer__c: Construction on the Golden Gate Bridge began in 1933 and ended in 1937.
Question__c: When was the Golden Gate Bridge Built?

Title: Where is the Golden Gate Bridge?
Summary: This article explains where the Golden Gate Bridge is located.
Answer__c: The Golden Gate Bridge is located in San Francisco, CA.  It connects the city of San Francisco to Marin County.
Question__c: Where is the Golden Gate Bridge located?

Title: How long is the Golden Gate Bridge?
Summary: This article explains the length of the Golden Gate Bridge.
Answer__c: The Golden Gate Bridge is 2,736 meters in length (about 1.7 miles).
Question__c: How long is the Golden Gate Bridge?

Title: Setup Your Web Portal
Summary: Learn how your customers can search your Knowledge Base and submit cases from your company's self-service site.
Answer__c:
To get started with Web Self-Service you will:


1. Create a new portal user


a. Search for the contact "Mark Land."



 


b. In the Contacts related list, select his name.





c. Replace the Email field with your email address. This is essential to enable the self-registration process.


d. Click Save.





2. Find the portal URL in the Setup area.


a. Click Your Name -> Setup.





b. In the left hand column, click "Customize" -> "Customer Portal" -> Settings.





c. Click on Trial Customer Portal.





d. Copy the "Login URL" link and open it in another browser.





3. Request a login to the customer portal


a. In the customer portal login page, enter your email address and click "Submit."





b. Go to your Inbox to receive login instructions.

The email you entered is your new username for the portal.  You received a temporary password in the email confirmation.

Go ahead and login with your new credentials.



Note: When you log into the portal you will automatically be logged out of any Salesforce.com sessions you have open within the same browser. If you would like to have both the customer portal view and the internal agent view inside of your Salesforce trial open at the same time, please use a new browser to log into the portal (Chrome vs. Firefox. vs. Safari, etc.)

4. Browse Knowledge Articles and Create a Case


a. Click on the "Articles" tab at the top.

 




b. Click on "Where is the Golden Gate Bridge?" article to preview it and close out when you're done.





c.  Click on the "Cases" Tab at the top.


d.  Click on the "Create New Case" button.





e. Fill in the fields and click Submit.





Great job! Your customers are now able to help themselves to important information!

Question__c: Learn how your customers can search your Knowledge Base and submit cases from your company's self-service site.

Title: Post a Question in a Service Community
Summary: Learn how to setup a customer community where customers can answer each other's questions and engage with your service agents and product experts.
Answer__c:
To get started with your online Community:


1. Grant Mark Land access to Chatter Answers - the Service Cloud's Q & A Community


a. Click on <your name> > Setup > Administration Setup > Manager Users > Users.








b. Click "Edit" for Mark Land.  If you don't see Mark Land as a user, please see Article 2 ("Setup Your Web Portal") to setup this user.





c. Check "Chatter Answer User."





d. Click Save.


2. Login to the portal as Mark Land


a. You should have already created a login for Mark Land, but if you haven't, see Article 2 ("Setup Your Web Portal") for detailed instructions.

Note: When you log into the portal you will automatically be logged out of any Salesforce.com sessions you have open within the same browser. If you would like to have both the customer portal view and the internal agent view inside of your Salesforce trial open at the same time, please use a new browser to log into the portal (Chrome vs. Firefox. vs. Safari, etc.)

b.  Once you've logged in, click on the "Chatter Answers" tab.





c. Ask the question "How long is the Golden Gate Bridge?"


d. Review the suggested answers and/or articles from the knowledge base.





e. Since none of the suggested solutions quite answer your specific question, you can post the question to the community.  Click "Post to the Community."  You will be prompted to add further information to your question.





f. Select "Sample Data" as the Topic.


g. Click "Post to the Community."


3.  View Case in Salesforce


The next step in this activity is to view the question from an agent or moderator's perspective.  Salesforce gives moderaters/agents the ability to view all open questions and respond with answers.


a. Log back into your Service Cloud console via login.salesforce.com.


b. Select the "Chatter Answers Moderation" view within Service Cloud.




c. Find the question from "Mark Land."





d. Answer the Question.





4. Optionally, log back into the portal to see the agent's response to the question


a. Check the answer from the agent is visible and selected as best answer.



Note: You will also receive an email when an answer is posted to one of you questions. 

Congratulations - you've just answered your first Community-generated question!

Title: View Service Reports and Dashboards
Summary: Learn how to use Reports & Dashboards to measure and track important metrics to your contact center.
Answer__c:
To get started with Reports and Dashboards you will:


1. Open the "Service Executive Dashboard"


a. In the navigator drop-down, click "Dashboards."





b. If you aren't directed there already, navigate to the "Service Cloud Executive" dashboard in the Search box.





c. Explore the content of the dashboard.


2. Add a filter based on the case field "type:"


a. Click "Edit" to start modifying the dashboard.





b. Click "Add filter."






c. In the "Field" field, type "Type" and select the second proposed option (Case Information > Type).





d. Add 2 filter options, so that Operator Equals "Trial" and "Sample Data" (use magnifying glass for assistance).





e. Click OK.


f. Click "Close" and then "Save & Close."





3. Drill into the report "Open Cases" and modify it with a new date range


a. ​Click on the graph "Open Cases," the full report will open. 





b. Change the date range option from "Custom" to "Last 120 days."





c. Click "Save" and "Save." 





d. Click on "Dashboard" in the navigator pane and click "Refresh" again.





Now you're on your way to being a dashboard whiz!

Title: Configuration: Add a custom field to cases
Summary: Learn how to add a custom field to a Case.
Answer__c:
To add a custom field to a Case:


a. Go to "Your Name" -> Setup -> App Setup -> Customize -> Cases -> Fields.







b.  Click "new" in the section "Case Custom Fields & Relationships."





c.  Select "formula" for the type.





d. Click Next.


e. In this example, we will add a custom field called "Case Age" and use a formula to calculate how many days the case has been open.  Enter "Case age" for the Field Label and select Number for the formula return type. 





f. Click Next


g. Enter "IF(IsClosed, ROUND(ClosedDate - CreatedDate, 0), ROUND((NOW() - CreatedDate),0))"





h. Click Next.


i. Click Next.


j. Click Save.




k. Go back to the service cloud console, open a case and click "view case details;" the case age field appears at the bottom of the details.


Now that you have the hang of it, go ahead and add all the custom fields that matter to your business!

Question__c: Learn how to add a custom field to a Case.

Title: Configuration: Enable Email-to-Case
Summary: Learn how to setup your email support channel.
Answer__c:
To enable Email-to-Case:


a. Go to <your name> > Setup > App Setup > Customize > Cases > Email-to-Case.







b.  Click Continue.

 

[Note: Email-to-Case is already enabled, however a "routing address" has to be added].


c.  Click New in the Routing Addresses sections.





d. Enter a name: "Support Cases."


Enter the email address you want to use (note: a verification email will be sent to this address; for testing purpose, choose an email address you can log into).





e. In the case origin drop down list, select "Email."





f. Click save and then OK.


g. In the next screen, locate and copy the email service address. Any email sent to this address will be converted as a case, which you can find in the "Email Cases" queue you created in the "Create a Queue" activity.  


Tip: Because the email address generated here is so long, most companies will create an email address such as "help@yourcompany.com" and automatically forward all emails to the long email address - so that the case is automatically created within Service Cloud.


Your email support channel is now up and running!

Question__c: Learn how to setup your email support channel.

Title: Configuration: Route Email Cases to New Queue
Summary: Learn how to route inbound email inquiries to the new case queue you just created.
Answer__c:
Make sure you have already enabled Email-To-Case and Setup a Queue before beginning this activity. See relevant Knowledge Articles for detailed instructions.


To Create a new routing assignment:


a. Go to <your name> > Setup > App Setup > Customize > Cases > Assignment Rules.







b.  Click New.





c.  Enter "Email Cases" for the rule name.





d.  Click Save.


e.  Click on the rule name.





f.  Click New in the rule entry section.





g.  Step 1: enter "1" in the Sort Order field.

Step 2: enter the criterion "Case: Case Origin equals Email."

Step 3: select "queue" in the drop-down list and enter "Email Cases."





h. Click Save.
 

i.  Click Edit.





j. Select "Active"





k. Click Save.

 
If the routing email address configured for email to case has been validated, then new case create from emails will now be associated to the Email Cases queue automatically.


Now go start solving some cases!

Title: Resolve a Case
Summary: This article will guide you through closing your first case and adding a comment to the case.
Answer__c:
To close your first case, you will:


1. View Knowledge Article 


a. In the Articles box to the right, click on the article "Resolve a Case."  The article will open in a new tab.  Close the tab when you're done previewing it. 





2. Email knowledge article to yourself


a. Once you've confirmed this is the correct article, click on the triangle next to the article and select "Email as Article PDF."





b. Click the "+" next to the Email drop-down menu.





c. Change the email "To" field to your email address.





d. Add a message within the body of the email, then click the green "Send Email" box.





3. Add an internal note to the case and close the case


a. In the left hand panel, click "Write Case Note."





b. In the text box, type "I have resolved the case" and click "Share."





c. Select "Change Status" in the left-hand side.





d. Change Status to "Closed" and click "Change Status."





Congratulations on closing your first case in the Service Cloud!

Title: Collaborate on a Case
Summary: Learn how Chatter enables your agents to collaborate on cases.
Answer__c:
1. Change your Chatter profile picture


a. Select "Chatter" in the navigator pane.





b. Click on the profile picture box.





c.  Hover over your picture, and click "Update."





d.  Choose a photo from your computer.





e. Click "Save."


2. Follow or subscribe to a case


a. Select "Cases" from the navigator pane.





b. Select "Sample Cases" from the drop down and click the case "When was the Golden Gate Bridge Built?"





c. Click "Follow" in the right hand corner.





3. Invite another agent to contribute to a case


a. Select "Write Case Note" in left navigation window.





b.  Using the "@" symbol, select "ServiceAgent."





c. Write a comment - "Can you help me solve this case?"





d. The comment will then be saved to the case feed below and the other user will receive an email notification.


4. Login as "ServiceAgent" to view the comment


a.  Click Setup under your name in the upper left corner.





b.  Click "Manage Users" and then "Users" in the left hand column.





c.  Find "ServiceAgent" and click the Login button next to the name.  You are now logged in as ServiceAgent.


 


d.  Click the "Back to Service Cloud Console" tab on the left.





e.  Select Chatter from the right-hand drop down.





f.  You will see the case comment right in your feed.  To respond, you click "Comment" or dive into the case by clicking the case number.






Great job! Don't stop collaborating now!

Title: Configuration: Hide the interaction log
Summary: Learn how to modify the Service Cloud User Interface.
Answer__c:
The default user interface of the Service Cloud Console has an Interaction Log in the footer of the console.  To Hide the Interaction Log in the Case View:


a. Go to "Your Name" -> Setup -> App Setup -> Customize-> Cases -> Page Layout.








b. In the section "Page Layouts for Case Feed Users," click the "Action" drop down list and select "Edit Detail View."





c. Click Layout Properties.





d. Uncheck "Interaction Log, Show in the Service Cloud console."





e. Click OK, then Save.


f. Click "back to the service cloud console."





g. Close all the case tabs open and reload the page.


h. Open a case to see the new case view without the interaction log.

Tip: If the Interaction Log is still there, log out of Salesforce and log back in.
 

Ta-da! The interaction log is now hidden. You can always re-enable it if you prefer.  


The video below will walk you through each of the steps:
Question__c: Learn how to modify the Service Cloud User Interface.

Title: Configuration: Create Additional Users
Summary: In this article, you will learn to add new users to your Service Cloud trial.
Answer__c:
Creating additional users will allow you to invite your coworkers to the trial. You can add up to three additional users.

Each username in the Salesforce platform must be unique; you cannot use a username that has been used to sign up before for any Salesforce product. The username and email do not need to be the same.


To add a user to your Service Cloud environment:


a. Go to "Your Name" -> Setup -> Manage Users -> Users







b. Click the "New User" button to the right.





c. Enter all fields marked as required: Last Name, Alias, Email, Username, Community Nickname.  

In the right column, select "Salesforce" for the User License type and "System Admin" for the Profile type.

Check the "Knowledge User" and "Service Cloud User" boxes. 

Tip: Press the "Tab" button to advance to next field. Many of the fields will auto-populate for you.





d. Uncheck the first two boxes in the "Newsletter Settings" box.


e. Make sure the last box is checked so your new user will immediately receive login credentials.





f. Click Save.


Remember, you can add up to three additional users!
